### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/embedder-openai`, `packages/plugins`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **12** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/embedder-openai/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/LICENSE`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **12** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/embedder-openai/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/LICENSE`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **17** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e46577b8cb7fffa6e348cad304196c1ab540683a` — the merge of head `78fff74e1e182c3e9432329e06e8a8a3dbf0b4fd` into base `f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e46577b8cb7fffa6e348cad304196c1ab540683a && git checkout e46577b8cb7fffa6e348cad304196c1ab540683a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba 78fff74e1e182c3e9432329e06e8a8a3dbf0b4fd && git checkout -B drift-repro f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba && git merge --no-ff 78fff74e1e182c3e9432329e06e8a8a3dbf0b4fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

What the diff removes or narrows, read from the tree at the head:

1. **A published package, whole.** `@objectstack/knowledge-ragflow` (`18.6.0`, not private, one `.` export) leaves the workspace: its nine files, its `pnpm-lock.yaml` importer and its `.changeset/config.json` fixed-group entry. Its entry exported `KnowledgeRagflowPlugin`, `KnowledgeRagflowPluginOptions`, `KnowledgeRagflowAdapter`, `KnowledgeRagflowAdapterOptions` and `FetchLike`, and registered adapter id `ragflow`. Right, per ruling R1. At the head `git ls-tree` finds nothing under the directory, and no `package.json`, tsconfig, workflow, vitest config or source file imports or names the package or any of the five exports. The only code-file hits left are comments in `knowledge.manifest.ts`, one frozen fixture line in `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs` (3456) and three rows in the generated `scripts/test-shard-timings.json`. Nothing deleted is still referenced.
2. **A settings accept set at a public door.** `knowledge.manifest.ts` loses the `ragflow` option of `adapter`, the `ragflow` group, the keys `ragflow_base_url`, `ragflow_api_key` (encrypted) and `ragflow_default_dataset`, and the `ragflow` branch of `knowledgeTestActionHandler`; `version` goes 2 to 3. Right, and the declared answers agree with the code: an undeclared key is `400 UNKNOWN_KEY` (`settings-routes.ts:435`), a value outside the option table is `invalid_option` (`settings-service.ts:3679`), and a stored `ragflow` reaches the handler's last line, `Unknown adapter`, sent as the `400` action-failure answer the PR body names (`settings-routes.ts:486`). The only reader of the `knowledge` namespace in the tree is `chunk_target` (`knowledge-service-plugin.ts:474`), so "no code ever read this setting" holds.
3. **Eleven locale bundles** lose the matching strings and nothing else (the two reflowed `options` lines in `ko.ts` and `zh-Hant.ts` drop only the `ragflow` entry). Right.
4. **No spec accept set moves.** The three `packages/spec/src` hunks are comments; `adapter` stays `z.string()` and `adapterConfig` stays declared. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `packages/spec/llms.txt` 78 to 77 follows the workspace.
5. **`adapterConfig` loses its last in-tree reader.** At the head no file under `packages/**/src` reads a source's `adapterConfig` (the one other hit is an unrelated `plugin-auth` comment). The key is still accepted and still handed to whatever adapter is registered, so it is not refused; it has no first-party reader. Right as a consequence of R1, and carried (see ③).
6. **Tests.** The new pin (a stored `ragflow`, with or without its old keys, answers `ok: false`, with a passing `turso` call beside it) and the absence pins match the code. The visibility count 87 to 83 matches the four removed `visible` predicates. The two fixture swaps to `turso` keep what each test asserts.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `service-settings`, `service-knowledge`, `embedder-openai`, `spec` and `skills` is right. AGENTS.md step 3: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The ruling says "no major". The repo is in changesets pre mode (`tag: next`) and the five packages sit in the fixed group that a pending major already moves, so the level changes nothing about the version consumers get. The retired package cannot be bumped and is not.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on both the PR body and the changeset, word for word the same, and agree with amendment 7183820019. The title carries `!`. `Check Changeset` is green on the head (three runs).
- The BREAKING paragraph declares both halves, the package and the three settings doors, and gives a path for each: stop registering `KnowledgeRagflowPlugin` and bind to `pgvector`, `turso`, `memory` or an own `IKnowledgeAdapter`; change a source's `adapter`; pick an adapter and save; delete the leftover rows by hand. The hand-deletion path names the right table (`sys_platform_setting`, the global rung this manifest's scope writes to) and the right handle column (`value_enc`, a `sec_` id), and matches `.changeset/33933-…` line 23.
- **The ADR-0087 marker is the wrong one: S1 in ④.** The gate is green because its prescription detector reads arrows, framed tables and migration headings, and this body's "What to do if you used it" list is plain sentences; `Metadata-protocol: none` keeps it clear of the outright refusal that `narrowed` would bring. No registry entry is owed either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note. SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

**Dogfood battery.** Verified from the os-dev report, not from CI. Card comment 7187346085 (by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, signed with thread session `session_01Utp6CaUMCSy2q88QhyTB9f`, the session amendment 7183625285 names) carries `dogfood_battery` opening with the full head sha `cb640fb26af60a9583c4f0ea8011e467db239f57`, then `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 487 files passed and 3 skipped, 4129 tests passed and 68 skipped. `card-37004/report.json` holds the same text. CI cannot confirm it: on a pull request the dogfood shard job is skipped by design (`ci.yml:2815`), so the green `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run on this head is the roll-up over a skipped matrix (the skipped run still carries its unexpanded matrix name) and `Dogfood Verify CLI` is skipped. The report is therefore the only evidence, and it has the shape `label-write --land` reads. Any commit on top that is not a merge of the base un-pins it.

**Check-runs on the head:** 66 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 in progress at the time of reading.

Dev deviations and out-of-scope findings, each answered:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx` left with three hits: accepted, release-owned path; carrier #37481 exists and is blocked on this card.
- `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` (three rows) and `partition-test-shards.mjs:3456` left: accepted. One is generated, one is a dated fixture; `Plan Test Core shards` is green with them in place. No card; the refresh workflow is the carrier.
- Surface additions (the `knowledge-service.ts` comment, the ADR-0161 cell, `llms.txt`, the `packages.mdx` count, the `embedder-openai` README paragraph): each is covered by an amendment or is prose; each is checked in ④ and holds.
- Silent unregistered adapter (measurement b): carrier #37479, p2. It matters more after this PR, since every source still naming `ragflow` now takes that path; the changeset says so in words.
- Blank select and no door to clear a removed key: carrier #37480, p2. See the escalation below.
- `lint.yml` step with an empty premise: carrier #37482.
- **`adapterConfig`, no new card: correct.** #37304 is the carrier. Its item 3 names `adapterConfig` as "a sixth removal by the same kit", on the stated premise that #37004 retires its only reader first, which is ADR-0161 K4 and row 2 of the execution table ("#37004 decides whether `adapterConfig` still has a reader at row 3"). #37304 is `pm:blocked` on other cards, not on this question.
- `.changeset/33933-…` now partly untrue for `ragflow_api_key`: this PR's changeset corrects it in the same release. Accepted.
- `file` and `http` source kinds with no ingesting adapter: pre-existing; #37304 item 3 retires both arms.

**Escalation E1 (security label).** `Security-touching` is `yes` and is meant. The diff changes credential behaviour: an encrypted settings key leaves the manifest, and with it the product's way to retire the stored value. The PR's own BREAKING paragraph and #37480 already state the facts, so nothing is added here. The seat adds the `security` label to the PR, and the seat or the maintainer decides whether the credential half of #37480 belongs under `security-findings.md` section 7 rather than a plain p2 finding. The dev report's `security_findings: none` does not match this reading.

**Serial order.** #37442 (open, draft, head `abf337bd`) shares 14 paths with this PR: `knowledge.manifest.ts`, the eleven locale files, `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Read hunk by hunk, the two diffs touch different lines everywhere; the closest pairs sit two unchanged lines apart (the `turso_url` help line against the `ragflow_*` key deletions in each locale file, and `## Wiring` against this PR's callout edit). No merge was run, so a clean textual merge is expected, not measured. #37442 adds no `ragflow` mention and does not touch the visibility pin. Whichever lands second merges `main` once and owes its own head record and, if it is this PR, a fresh battery. #37310 is a blocked card with no PR; it rewrites eval cases 3 and 9 and must start from this PR's `pgvector` case 3. #37304 (blocked, no PR) rewrites the same `supportKb` block in the skill and lands after. `origin/main` has moved 11 files past this PR's base and none of them is in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**S1 (should-fix) — the changeset holds `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` for a deleted published package, against ADR-0087.** Two rules meet here. ADR-0087's addendum says that category "is refused by a body that carries a migration prescription", and this body carries one: "Stop registering `KnowledgeRagflowPlugin` and remove the dependency. Bind your sources to…" and "Change the source's `adapter`" are instructions to rewrite consumer code. ADR-0087 D9, as amended 2026-10-27 on the maintainer's ruling (PR #26365, comment 6439038287), names the disposition for exactly this shape, "a published package deleted at HEAD is retired whole": `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/knowledge-ragflow#*)`, with one FROM line naming the package. AGENTS.md step 3 separately asks a breaking changeset that removes an export for a FROM to TO mapping and a one-line fix, and the body has the fix only as prose. The marker's own justification argues the settings half alone and is silent on the five retired exports. The gate is green by a detector miss, which is the failure the seventh category was added to close. The outcome does not change (no ledger entry is owed) and nothing ships wrong, which is why the grade stops here. The fix is in the changeset alone: carry the D9 marker with its one FROM line for the package, and keep the settings half's argument beside it; if one marker cannot carry both halves, two changesets, one per half. Not measured here: whether the gate accepts the combined body, since no gate was re-run.

No must-fix.

Per `hits` file:

- **`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`** — holds, sentence by sentence. The three adapter packages exist and are published; their default ids are `memory`, `pgvector` (`pgvector-adapter.ts:180`) and `turso` (`turso-adapter.ts:244`). All three declare `capabilities = { chunks: true }`, and the service cuts passages only for such an adapter (`knowledge-service.ts:297`), so "any other adapter receives whole documents" is true. The default strategy is `recursive` (`splitter.ts:106`). The `os:check` example parses unchanged apart from the adapter string. No hunk teaches permission or credential behaviour.
- **`skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`, case 3** — holds. The pgvector adapter stores document metadata and applies a metadata-equality `filter` in SQL (`pgvector-adapter.ts:444`), so "filter by `category` at search time" with `metadataFields: ['category']` is a real path, which it was not on the retired adapter. The assertions are unchanged and still fit the expected answer. Rewriting rather than dropping the case keeps the only object-source case with `where`, `metadataFields` and `refresh`.
- **`.github/workflows/lint.yml`** — the new clause holds. `DEBT` and `TEST_DEBT` are both `{}` at the head (`check-type-check-coverage.mjs:845`, `:1135`), and the gate's closure roots are exactly their keys (`:4371`), so the closure is empty today. The `run:` line is untouched.
- **ADR-0161, the `adapterConfig` cell** — holds. The dead anchor is gone, the four keys are the ones the retired `extractRagflowOptions` read, and "no adapter in the tree reads it now" is true at the head. No decision text moves; K4's rule and row 2 of the execution table are unchanged and now resolve to the removal #37304 carries.
- **The three `packages/spec/src` comment hunks** — hold. Each names adapters that exist in the tree; no schema, `describe()` text or type moves.

Implementing files:

- **`knowledge.manifest.ts`** agrees with its own new header paragraph and with the changeset, line for line (see ① item 2). The handler comment's "no adapter package reads this namespace or registers `knowledge/test`" is true at the head.
- **`scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`, `regen-artifacts.mjs`** and the four other scripts: comment edits, one self-test URL and one removed ledger row for a file that no longer exists. `Type Check · debt ledger` and the tooling self-test lanes are green.
- **`embedder-openai` README** — the rewritten paragraph is true: both vector plugins take `embedder?: IEmbedder` and fall back to the kernel's `embedder` service, which `KnowledgeServicePlugin` registers from the `ai.embedder_*` settings; the memory adapter takes none.
- **`content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`** — the Plugins row lists 18 names and says 18.

Nits, none of which moves correctness or the contract:

- N1 — `lint.yml`: the unchanged sentence right after the hunk ("Delete this step and the lane's green starts depending on that one manifest…") is no longer true once the hunk itself says the closure is empty. Carrier #37482.
- N2 — ADR-0161: the edited cell says "#37004 retired that package" while lines 63, 212, 216, 342, 360 and 417 still say it "is being retired" or "retires", and the Readings table (513, 522) cites the deleted file by line number. Dated readings; left to the ADR owner.
- N3 — the skill's example is now `pgvector`, and the skill never says the vector adapters need an embedder (without one they answer `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with the fix named, so the failure is loud). The file is 3 tokens under its ceiling. Carrier #37310, with eval case 9's "the adapter that takes the service's passages", which three adapters now are.
- N4 — `knowledge-source.zod.ts` keeps "(Dify, Vectara)" on `embedding` where the skill row dropped the engine names. Harmless; `embedding` leaves in #37304.
- N5 — the skill and `protocol/knowledge.mdx` still present `adapterConfig` as live configuration with no in-tree reader left. True for an adapter a deployment writes itself; carriers #37304 and #37310.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `cb640fb26af60a9583c4f0ea8011e467db239f57`
**REWORK**: L1, seat repo:objectstack#5. Contract record 7187805241 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, verified on the transcript) reads **PASS** with one should-fix open, and the queue guard refuses a record while it is open. The narrowing is real, fully declared, and nothing deleted is still referenced.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 50 files (+159/−7041), `Fixes #37004`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `!` title, patch changeset. Tier H (skills/**, `lint.yml`, an ADR cell, over 3000 lines). 66 success, 13 expected skips, 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: ruling 7134290286 R1. Retire the package whole, in one PR, as a patch.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **S1.** The changeset carries `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, but its "What to do if you used it" list is a migration prescription, which that category refuses. ADR-0087 D9 (amended 2026-10-27, ruling on PR #26365) names the disposition for a published package deleted at HEAD: `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/knowledge-ragflow#*)` with one FROM line. Carry that marker for the package half and keep the settings half's argument beside it. If one marker cannot carry both, split it into two changesets. Run `check-adr-0087-registration` on the result.
   - **Dogfood battery.** The fix is a non-merge commit, so the battery pinned to `cb640fb2` no longer covers the head. Re-run it on the new head and update the report. `label-write` reads it.
   - The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations** (nits, record only):
   - N1: the `lint.yml` sentence after the hunk (carrier #37482).
